expectations.description: Does NOT simply validate the cross-lagged paths as clean evidence of within-person bidirectional causal dynamics
expectations.evidence: The response explicitly states 'the cross-lagged paths reflect a *within-person* relationship... The standard CLPM does not do this' and includes a table showing 'This reflects a **within-person** dynamic | ❌ No | Standard CLPM cannot isolate within-person effects', directly refusing to validate the cross-lagged paths as clean evidence of within-person bidirectional causal dynamics.

expectations.description: Explains that the standard CLPM cannot separate within-person dynamics from stable between-person trait co-occurrence — the cross-lagged paths reflect a mixture of both
expectations.evidence: The response explicitly states: 'The standard cross-lagged panel model (CLPM) you ran in lavaan does not partial out stable, trait-like individual differences... the cross-lagged paths regress the total score at T2 on the total score at T1 — a mixture of: Between-person variance: Chronically lonelier people also tend to be chronically more depressed. This stable covariance bleeds into your cross-lagged estimates. Within-person variance: The genuine fluctuations around each person's own average level over time.' It also cites Hamaker et al. (2015) who 'demonstrated formally that cross-lagged coefficients from a standard CLPM are a weighted mixture of the two sources.'

expectations.description: Names the Random Intercept Cross-Lagged Panel Model (RI-CLPM) as the appropriate model for isolating within-person effects, citing Hamaker, Kuiper and Grasman (2015) or equivalent
expectations.evidence: The response explicitly names the RI-CLPM and cites 'Hamaker, Kuiper, & Grasman (2015, Psychological Methods)' multiple times, stating it 'demonstrated formally that cross-lagged coefficients from a standard CLPM are a weighted mixture of the two sources' and that the RI-CLPM adds random intercepts to isolate within-person effects.

expectations.description: Explains the RI-CLPM mechanism: random intercepts absorb each person's stable trait level, leaving cross-lagged paths that operate on within-person deviations from the individual's own mean
expectations.evidence: The response explicitly states: 'The Random Intercept Cross-Lagged Panel Model (RI-CLPM) — Hamaker et al. (2015) — adds random intercepts for each person, which absorb stable between-person differences. The cross-lagged paths then operate *only* on within-person deviations from each person's own trait level.' It further illustrates the within-person interpretation: 'When a person is *more lonely than their own average* at time t, they are subsequently *more depressed than their own average* at time t+1.'

expectations.description: Notes that in many published datasets, RI-CLPM cross-lagged paths are substantially attenuated or become non-significant compared to CLPM estimates
expectations.evidence: The response explicitly states: 'The RI-CLPM commonly attenuates or eliminates cross-lagged paths that appear significant in standard CLPMs... It is not rare to find that the within-person paths shrink toward zero or become non-significant.' (parse truncation corrected on manual review)

expectations.description: Recommends re-estimating the model as an RI-CLPM before drawing within-person causal conclusions — this may be done in lavaan or via the riclpm package
expectations.evidence: The response explicitly recommends 'Refit as an RI-CLPM' and provides lavaan code for implementing the Random Intercept Cross-Lagged Panel Model, directly satisfying the assertion about recommending re-estimation as an RI-CLPM before drawing within-person causal conclusions and doing so in lavaan.
